image-sampling.scope: Central horizontal sample rows in declared endpoint windows, using prior black-grid geometry. Models are library/coordinate hypotheses, not vendor implementation or general production corrections. All 56 models per row and all failures retained.

failures.description: Direct slicing of a pikepdf array failed before any PDF was written. Converted the MediaBox to a Python list; a new output directory retained the initial empty directory. No Wine session was restarted.

All tested colored patterns lose all interior ink under Wine, including both gray path positives. Other renderer checks paint the content; this is a scoped Wine/PDF route failure, not a universal absence of pattern support.

Y reversal alone regresses both gray-grid views and two actual 100% image-only views. Combining it with target extents regresses all nine actual views relative to extent-only. No generic production correction is adopted.

limitations: Tiling, clipping and hairline results concern only the tested PDFs/profile. Pattern-positive loss prevents a universal parser-support claim.
Central horizontal samples become equal after the declared extent change; no tested resampling model explains all native rows, and no vendor decoder or API is identified.
Five complete original-control frames become exact only with target-zoom extents plus Y reversal. These extents change physical geometry and cross-zoom gray frames lose equality.

The actual source uses negative vertical image matrices and page-crossing image positions; the new gray/asymmetric controls have positive vertical matrices. Sign and clipping remain confounded and require independent source controls.

Original JPEG resources remain embedded, but the painted diagnostic resources contain full-resolution lossless-Flate samples. Pixel identity means inverse-transform identity of Pillow-decoded samples, not identical rendering in every PDF engine.
MuPDF is a secondary implementation check, not the requested source of truth. Its JPEG-to-Flate and orientation pixels may differ; those differences are retained.
No production implementation, new 77-page conversion/visual sweep, or native/Node/browser parity run is claimed. #543/#541/#406 remain open.
